proposal.title: Pelorvul: a route origin validation toolkit
proposal.summary: Pelorvul builds a route origin validation toolkit for operators of community networks.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Many small networks accept route announcements without checking their origin. Operators of community networks depend on routing security every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a route origin validation toolkit called Pelorvul. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Routing security is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/pelorvul/pelorvul, which 16 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on routing security for 11 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/pelorvul/pelorvul. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 98600.00 EUR for 76 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Many small networks accept route announcements without checking their origin. Operators of community networks depend on routing security every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a route origin validation toolkit called Pelorvul. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Routing security is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/pelorvul/pelorvul, which 16 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on routing security for 11 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/pelorvul/pelorvul. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 98600.00 EUR for 76 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.
